scope: All 21 battlefield scene prop assets in batch01–06; map icons excluded. Batch04 has no scene props.
reviewMethod: Visually reviewed all 21 actual PNGs in three contact sheets on a neutral gray backdrop, with an additional enlarged alpha-threshold crop review of the two early shared prop layers.

summary.finding: No material, camera or rendering-style replacement is warranted. Regional palette, night lighting and interior emissive accents are coherent intentional differences. Existing alpha, canvas margin and shared-layer layout limitations are separate production concerns.

items.reason: Weathered canvas and mossy chipped stone use matte painterly shading and a low three-quarter view. Warm daylight and lantern accents fit the day variant; the wide shared-layer layout is a compositing limitation, not a style mismatch.
Matches the day layer in canvas treatment, broken masonry, camera and painted texture. Cool blue ambient light with warm lanterns is intentional night lighting, not a palette outlier.
Chipped, moss-flecked masonry has tactile matte detail, restrained color and soft directional shading consistent with the regional stone props. Near-frontal low camera suits an arch.
Frayed gray canvas, sagging fabric, rope and rough poles share the weathered handpainted material language; soft light and a low three-quarter camera fit the benchmark.
Broken fluted stone has granular matte wear, restrained ochre-gray color and soft upper-left illumination; camera agrees with the prop family.
Rough timber, rope bindings and frayed canvas have tactile matte wear with coherent soft lighting and low three-quarter presentation.
Angular basalt uses chipped, dry stone texture and muted charcoal values; the slightly raised view remains within the three-quarter prop family.
Broken soot-dark stone and rusty iron maintain matte handpainted material detail, grounded silhouette and consistent directional lighting.
Splintered gray timber, moss and dull iron bands match the weathered tactile treatment. Visible deck top is appropriate to a low jetty and does not constitute a camera outlier.
Splintered planks and curved ribs use subdued coastal gray timber and matte painted wear; the exposed interior reads consistently in three-quarter view.
Twisted bark, moss and fern details retain the restrained handpainted finish; green biome accents and the low natural silhouette fit the family.
Weathered wood, moss and chipped roof shingles share the matte tactile finish and low three-quarter architecture treatment.
Dull rusty iron and chipped stone pillars use consistent weathering, soft highlights and a grounded three-quarter view; no plastic shine or heavy contour.
Timber grain, chipped coal and rusted metal retain the benchmark material language. Wheel and band highlights remain dull and directional.
Rough masonry, snow and icicles are painted with tactile matte detail; cool snow light is intentional regional coloration, with a consistent low camera.
Chipped stone and snow use granular matte paint and soft upper-left illumination; the cold palette is coherent with the Pale Marches.
Rough plaster, timber and stone have restrained handpainted wear with soft upper-left lighting and a grounded three-quarter camera.
Soot-dark masonry, dull roof iron and restrained window glow match the tactile dark fantasy benchmark; warmer interior accents are intentional.
Silvered timber, patched roof, rope and nets share matte coastal weathering and the grounded three-quarter camera used by the settlement family.
Mossy shingles, gnarled timber and worn steps have consistent tactile handpainted texture, low camera and subdued woodland greens.
Snow-covered chipped masonry keeps the family's matte surface detail and low three-quarter camera; cool regional lighting is intentional.
